title: Signals, Signs & Markings
summary: Posted limits assume ideal conditions, so never exceed them, and ride slower whenever traffic, road surface, weather, visibility, or pedestrians and cyclists call for it.

Where no other limit is posted, the manual treats riding over 20 mph in school zones, 30 mph in thickly settled or business districts, 40 mph outside those districts, or 50 mph on highways outside them as unreasonable, and it sets a 45 mph minimum on interstates and other limited-access highways.

A steady red light, or a red arrow for traffic headed the arrow's way, means stop; after a full stop and yielding you may turn right on red unless NO TURN ON RED is posted, but a left on red is allowed only from one one-way street onto another.
Treat a flashing red like a STOP sign, stop for a steady yellow if you safely can, proceed carefully on a flashing yellow, and handle a blacked-out signal as an all-way stop.
On a steady green, go only after yielding and only if you can clear the intersection without blocking it; a green arrow permits a turn in the arrow's direction.
Riders must give way to any pedestrian stepping into or walking in a crosswalk along their path, and to pedestrians whenever their own signal shows red, alone or together with yellow.
Never stop with your motorcycle across a crosswalk, and never overtake a vehicle that is slowing down or stopped for a pedestrian.

Sign colors: red is stop, yellow general warning, orange construction or maintenance, black and white regulation, green direction, blue motorist services, and brown recreational, historic or scenic sites.

Sign shapes: octagon is stop, downward triangle yield, diamond warning, five-sided school zone, round railroad crossing, pennant no-passing zone, upright rectangle regulation, wide rectangle guide information, and shield interstate highway.

At a STOP sign come to a full stop (slowing is not enough) behind any stop line or painted crosswalk, at a four-way stop the first vehicle into the intersection goes first, and at a YIELD sign slow down, let others go first, and stop only if traffic requires it.
Orange work-zone signs call for extra caution because conditions there change quickly, and you must obey any flagger or police officer directing traffic.

A round yellow warning sign means a railroad crossing is ahead; if the crossing lights flash, stop at least 15 feet from the gate or light post, stay stopped until the gate is up and the flashing ends, and never ride around a gate that is down.

White lines separate same-direction lanes: cross a broken one to change lanes after signaling, a solid one only to avoid a hazard, a double solid one never, and a painted white diamond marks a restricted lane such as HOV, bus or bicycle only.
Yellow lines separate opposing traffic: you may cross to pass only when the broken line is on your side, and you may cross a double solid yellow only to turn left.

questions.q: The posted limit is 40 mph, but it is raining and the road is wet. How fast should you ride?
options: At 40 mph, since posted limits already take bad weather into account
At exactly 40 mph, since riding below a posted limit is not allowed
Up to 45 mph, to keep pace with the flow of traffic
Slower than 40 mph, at a speed suited to the conditions
questions.explanation: Posted limits are set for ideal conditions. When rain or another hazard is present you must slow below the limit to a speed that is reasonable for the conditions, and you may never go above it.

questions.q: According to the manual, what is the minimum speed on Massachusetts interstate and limited-access highways?
options: 35 mph
45 mph
50 mph
55 mph
questions.explanation: The manual gives 45 mph as the lowest speed allowed on Massachusetts interstates and other limited-access highways. Their posted maximums range from 50 to 65 mph.

questions.q: Unless a different limit is posted, riding faster than what speed in a school zone is not considered reasonable and proper?
options: 10 mph
15 mph
20 mph
30 mph
questions.explanation: Near schools the default limit is 20 mph. It may be marked with flashing yellow lights or apply only during certain hours, so watch carefully for school zone signs.

questions.q: Unless a different limit is posted, riding faster than what speed in a thickly settled or business district is not considered reasonable and proper?
options: 20 mph
30 mph
35 mph
40 mph
questions.explanation: When no other limit is posted, the manual's defaults are 20 mph in school zones, 30 mph in thickly settled or business districts, 40 mph outside them, and 50 mph on highways outside them. Many Massachusetts cities and towns have since lowered the 30 mph default to 25 mph, so watch the signs; for the test, the manual's figure is 30.

questions.q: When does the manual allow a left turn on a steady red light?
options: Never; Massachusetts does not allow left turns on a red light
From a two-way street onto a one-way street, after stopping and yielding
From a one-way street onto another one-way street, after stopping and yielding
Any time no oncoming traffic is in sight, after slowing down and checking
questions.explanation: A left on red is permitted only when going from one one-way street onto another, and only after a full stop and yielding to pedestrians and vehicles.

questions.q: A flashing red traffic light means the same as which of these?
options: A STOP sign
A YIELD sign
A warning sign
A DO NOT ENTER sign
questions.explanation: Treat a flashing red light just like a STOP sign: stop completely, follow the right-of-way rules, and continue only when it is safe.

questions.q: What does a steady yellow traffic light mean?
options: The light is about to turn green, so get ready to go
It is only a warning, so you may proceed with caution
Speed up to clear the intersection before it turns red
The signal is changing to red; stop if you can do so safely
questions.explanation: A steady yellow warns that red is next, so stop if you can do it safely. A rider who is already waiting at the intersection or stop line must not go. Do not confuse it with a flashing yellow, which is only a warning to proceed with caution.

questions.q: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?
options: Come to a complete stop, then go when it is safe
The signal is about to change from green to red
Proceed with caution and stay alert
Stop and wait until the light turns green
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow is a warning, not an order to stop: continue carefully, stay alert and check both directions as you cross. A steady yellow is the one that means the signal is changing to red.

questions.q: Your light is green, but traffic is backed up on the far side of the intersection. What should you do?
options: Wait until there is room to get completely through the intersection
Go ahead, since the green light gives you the right-of-way
Enter the intersection and wait inside it until traffic moves
Pull partway into the intersection so cross traffic sees you
questions.explanation: A green light lets you go only after yielding and only if you can clear the intersection completely. Never pull in where you would end up blocking it.

questions.q: You reach an intersection where the traffic signals are completely dark and not working. What must you do?
options: Slow down, and go through without stopping if no one is coming
Proceed with caution, as you would at a flashing yellow light
Keep going if you are on the busier of the two roads
Treat it as if there were stop signs in every direction
questions.explanation: Blacked-out signals turn the intersection into an all-way stop: stop, then go when it is safe. If the signals are flashing instead, follow the flashing-light rules.

questions.q: You are turning right on a green light, and a pedestrian has just stepped into the crosswalk on the street you are turning onto. What must you do?
options: Complete the turn, since the green light gives you the right-of-way
Yield and let the pedestrian cross
Speed up to finish the turn before the pedestrian reaches your lane
Sound your horn to warn the pedestrian, then make the turn
questions.explanation: A green light lets you go only after yielding, and riders must give way to anyone stepping into or walking in a crosswalk along their path.

questions.q: Which of these does the manual say a motorcycle rider must never do?
options: Yield to a pedestrian who is entering a crosswalk
Come to a complete stop before turning right on red
Let the motorcycle block a crosswalk
Stop behind the stop line at a STOP sign
questions.explanation: One of the laws for riders is that your motorcycle must never block a crosswalk. The other three choices are all things the manual requires you to do.

questions.q: Your traffic signal is showing red and yellow lights at the same time. What must you do?
options: Yield to pedestrians, as you must at a red light
Go ahead, since pedestrians must wait while your signal shows yellow
Treat it like a flashing yellow and continue without yielding
Turn right without stopping, since the yellow overrides the red
questions.explanation: The rider laws require you to give way to pedestrians whenever your signal shows red, including when red and yellow are lit together.

questions.q: The vehicle in the lane next to yours is slowing down for a pedestrian at a crosswalk ahead. What should you do?
options: Pass it quickly before the pedestrian reaches your lane
Pass it once it has come to a complete stop
Sound your horn and continue past it
Stay back and do not pass it
questions.explanation: The rider laws forbid overtaking any vehicle that is slowing down or stopped for a pedestrian, so stay back instead of going around it.

questions.q: You have stopped at a red light and want to turn right, and no sign prohibits it. A pedestrian is walking in the crosswalk in your path. What must you do?
options: Turn now, since you have already come to a complete stop
Wait and let the pedestrian cross before you turn
Turn quickly, before the pedestrian reaches your side of the road
Go ahead, since pedestrians must wait for vehicles turning on red
questions.explanation: Stopping does not end your duty: with a red signal you must still give way to pedestrians, and a right on red is legal only after a full stop and yielding to anyone in your path.

questions.q: What does a brown traffic sign indicate?
options: Motorist services such as gas, food and lodging
A recreational, historic or scenic site
Construction or maintenance work ahead
Directions to highway exits and interchanges
questions.explanation: Sign colors are coded: brown marks recreational, historic and scenic sites, blue marks motorist services, green gives directions, and orange warns of construction or maintenance.

questions.q: At an intersection where every approach has a STOP sign marked 4-WAY or ALL WAY, which vehicle has the right-of-way?
options: The vehicle on the left
A motorcycle, since it can clear the intersection fastest
The first vehicle in the intersection
The largest vehicle, since it needs the most room
questions.explanation: With an ALL WAY (or 4-WAY) plate under each STOP sign, everyone approaching must stop, and the vehicle that is first in the intersection goes first.

questions.q: You see an orange diamond-shaped sign ahead. What does it tell you?
options: A school zone is just ahead, so watch for children
Construction or maintenance work is ahead, so take extra care
A recreational or scenic area is ahead, so watch for its entrance
Motorist services such as gas and food are available
questions.explanation: Orange signs warn of construction or maintenance work. They may show familiar warning symbols, but they call for extra caution because conditions around work zones can change fast.

questions.q: What does a yellow pennant-shaped sign (a sideways triangle pointing right) mark?
options: A school zone
A railroad crossing ahead
A place where you must yield
A no-passing zone
questions.explanation: On the manual's chart of sign shapes, the pennant marks a no-passing zone, meaning you must not pass by crossing the yellow line there. A yield sign is a triangle pointing down, not sideways.

questions.q: What does a five-sided sign, shaped like a house with a pointed top, indicate?
options: A school zone
A no-passing zone
A railroad crossing ahead
A highway rest area
questions.explanation: On the manual's chart of sign shapes, the five-sided, house-shaped outline is the school zone sign. Pennants mark no-passing zones and round signs mark railroad crossings.

questions.q: The red lights at a railroad crossing start flashing as you approach. What must you do?
options: Stop at least 15 feet from the gate or light post and wait until the gate rises and the lights stop
Stop at least 5 feet from the tracks, then cross as soon as you can see that no train is coming
Stop at least 15 feet from the gate, then ride around it if you can see that no train is coming
Slow down, check both ways, and cross quickly before the gate has come all the way down
questions.explanation: Once the lights flash, you must halt no closer than 15 feet to the gate or light post and stay put until the gate is up and the flashing ends. Going around a lowered gate is never allowed, even if no train is visible.

questions.q: When may you cross a single solid white lane line?
options: Whenever you have signaled and it is safe
Only to pass a slower vehicle
Never, under any circumstances
Only when you must, to avoid a hazard
questions.explanation: A single solid white line marks the road edge or divides same-direction lanes, and you should cross it only if needed to avoid a hazard. A broken white line is the one you may cross to change lanes after signaling.

questions.q: Two solid white lines run side by side between two lanes going the same direction. When may you cross them?
options: After signaling, whenever it is safe
Only when you must, to avoid a hazard
Never; crossing them is prohibited
Only to make a left turn
questions.explanation: The manual flatly forbids crossing two solid white lines. A single solid white line may be crossed only to avoid a hazard, and a broken white line may be crossed to change lanes after signaling.

questions.q: The center of a two-way road is marked with a double yellow line: the line nearest you is solid and the far line is broken. What does this mean for you?
options: You may not cross it to pass
You may cross it to pass when it is safe
Traffic from both directions may cross it to pass when safe
It separates two lanes moving in the same direction
questions.explanation: With a solid-and-broken pair, the line nearest you decides: solid on your side means you may not cross, while broken on your side lets you cross only to pass when it is safe.

questions.q: When may you cross a double solid yellow center line?
options: To pass a slow vehicle when the road ahead is clear
Only to make a left turn, when it is safe
Never, for any reason
To pass a vehicle that has stopped for a pedestrian
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines bar passing from both directions; the only time you may cross them is to make a left turn when it is safe.

questions.q: What does a white diamond painted in a traffic lane mean?
options: A pedestrian crosswalk is just ahead, so be ready to stop
Passing is permitted in this section of road
A railroad crossing is ahead, so slow down and look for trains
The lane is restricted, such as to HOV, buses or bicycles
questions.explanation: A painted white diamond warns that the lane has a special restriction, such as being for high-occupancy vehicles, buses or bicycles only.
